content.comment_body: Hello, I am experiencing difficulties with a [product_name] device when it is placed in a different network segment, since it lacks an option to set a gateway, which limits its ability to communicate outside its subnet. Currently, I can configure only the IP address and subnet mask, but not the gateway. Is it possible to allow gateway configuration? It seems outdated for an IP device today to be missing such a fundamental setting, as the gateway is one of the essential parameters for networking. We operate within a large network environment, split into two areas—one for general use, the other for technical operations. There are more than 400 buildings under control, and remote access to the device is required for monitoring, updating, and modifying settings. At present, onsite intervention is needed, which is impractical. Regards, [user_name], System integrator [company_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user highlights a significant limitation with a [product_name] module, unable to set a gateway IP. This restricts remote device management and monitoring—an essential feature for large, segmented networks. The lack of gateway configuration impacts operational efficiency and usability, particularly for system integrators managing extensive installations.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the ability to configure an IP gateway alongside the IP address and subnet mask to enable basic remote network communication. They anticipate modern networking capabilities in IP-enabled devices for effective and efficient system management.
